lines.text: What if India stopped making medicine… tomorrow?
Vik bets his whole chocolate stash that nobody would even notice.
But Gus just walks Nik into a pharmacy in London, and taps the shelf.
About one in every four medicines here comes from India, and they blink out of existence.
So they jump to America, where about four in ten generic prescriptions are Indian, and those boxes vanish too.
Then to a village clinic, where most of UNICEF's children's vaccines were made in India… and the cold box goes empty.
Now Vik is sweating, but he asks the real question: why India?
Gus holds up two pills that do exactly the same job.
When a medicine's patent runs out, anyone can make it, and Indian factories learned to make the same pill for a tiny fraction of the price, by the billions.
In two thousand and one, one Indian company took an HIV treatment that cost ten thousand dollars a year, and offered it for under a dollar a day.
And Vik? He hands over his chocolate… then reaches for a headache pill. Made in India.
So next time you open a medicine box, check the back, and ask…
